title: Joshua's Farewell Warning to Israel
overview: Near the end of his life, Joshua gathers Israel's leaders to remind them that God fought for them and to warn them to stay loyal to God alone.

parts.label: Joshua credits God (vv. 1-5)
parts.note: An aging Joshua calls the leaders together, possibly at Shiloh, where Israel's central place of worship stood, though the text does not say where. He gives the victories entirely to God rather than himself and says God will also push out the peoples still living in the land.

parts.label: Stay on the path (vv. 6-8)
parts.note: Joshua urges them to keep the law given through Moses without drifting either way. In practice that meant having nothing to do with the local gods: not calling on them, not naming them in oaths, not bowing to them.

parts.label: Why loyalty makes sense (vv. 9-11)
parts.note: Saying one Israelite could chase off a thousand is a bold way of claiming their success came from God, not their own strength. Joshua sums up everything he asks in one command: love the LORD your God.

parts.label: The danger of mixing in (vv. 12-13)
parts.note: Joshua warns against alliances and marriages with the peoples who remain in the land. If Israel does this, he says, God will stop driving those peoples out, and they will become like traps, whips and thorns in the eye until Israel loses the land.

parts.label: Promises cut both ways (vv. 14-16)
parts.note: Joshua says every good promise God made has come true, so God's threats of disaster will come true just as surely if Israel serves other gods. Many scholars think this speech was shaped with Israel's later exile from the land in view, which made the warning read like a forecast.

think: When someone near the end of their life warns you about what really matters, what makes their words worth taking seriously, or not?
